entries.displayName: RS-BA1 v2 — direct to radio LAN port

stationTarget.label: Radio's IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: This is where the Station sends traffic after it comes out of the tunnel. The Station is already on the same LAN as your radio, so this is the radio's ordinary local address -- not a Tailscale address, and not your public IP.
stationTarget.howToFind: On the radio: MENU -> SET -> Network -> IP Address. Set a fixed address rather than DHCP; if the radio's lease changes, these rules point at nothing.
stationTarget.ifWrong: The rules will bind normally and the Status column will read 'Listening'. Nothing will report an error. Remote Utility will simply fail to connect, or hang at the login step.

clientNotes: Remote Utility -> Server List: address 127.0.0.1, control port 50001
Leave 'Server Setting' completely blank on the client side
The Radio List fills itself in on the first successful connect
stationNotes: No station-side software required -- radio serves RS-BA1 directly
radioNotes: Set a fixed LAN IP on the radio (do not rely on DHCP)
Register a Network User with a password in the radio's Network menu

stationTarget.label: RS-BA1 Server PC address
stationTarget.why: The Remote Utility server runs on this PC. If it's the same machine as RWK Station, use 127.0.0.1. If it's a different PC on the Station's LAN, use that PC's LAN address.
stationTarget.howToFind: If the server is on the Station PC itself: 127.0.0.1. Otherwise: run ipconfig on the server PC and use its IPv4 address.
stationTarget.ifWrong: Remote Utility will fail to connect with no useful diagnostic. The rules will show 'Listening' normally.

clientNotes: Remote Utility -> Server List: address 127.0.0.1, control port 50001
Leave 'Server Setting' completely blank on the client side
The Remote Utility server must be RUNNING on the station PC (it is a foreground program)
stationNotes: RS-BA1 Remote Utility Server must be running on the station PC
The server is a foreground program, not a Windows service
radioNotes: Radio must be connected to the server PC via USB or CI-V cable

stationTarget.label: Radio's IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: wfview connects directly to the radio's LAN port using Icom's native protocol (same ports as RS-BA1).
stationTarget.howToFind: On the radio: MENU -> SET -> Network -> IP Address.
stationTarget.ifWrong: wfview will show 'Connecting...' and eventually time out.

clientNotes: wfview -> Radio Access = Network, hostname 127.0.0.1
Ports 50001/50002/50003, radio username and password as set in radio's Network menu
radioNotes: Set a fixed LAN IP on the radio
Register a Network User with a password

stationTarget.label: TS-890S IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: The Station sends control and audio here after traffic leaves the tunnel. This is the radio's ordinary LAN address -- not a Tailscale address.
stationTarget.howToFind: On the radio: LAN menu -> IP Address. Set it manually; a DHCP lease change will silently break these rules.
stationTarget.ifWrong: Both rules bind and show 'Listening'. ARCP-890 fails to connect with no useful diagnostic.

clientNotes: Connection type: KNS (Directly to TS-890S)
IP address: 127.0.0.1
Leave the MAC address field BLANK -- use the Internet-mode configuration, not the LAN-mode one
Tick 'Use TS-890S Built-in VoIP'
radioNotes: KNS menu 1: KNS Operation (LAN Connector) = On (Internet)
Modulation Source: DATA SEND audio input = LAN

stationTarget.label: ARHP host PC address
stationTarget.why: ARHP runs on a PC at the station connected to the radio via USB. If that PC is the RWK Station, use 127.0.0.1.
stationTarget.howToFind: If ARHP runs on the Station PC itself: 127.0.0.1. Otherwise run ipconfig on the ARHP PC.
stationTarget.ifWrong: ARCP will fail to connect to ARHP.

clientNotes: ARCP -> ARHP port number: 50000 (or whatever you set)
ARVP-10R -> connect to 127.0.0.1 port 33550
stationNotes: ARHP must be running on the station PC (foreground program)
Radio connected via USB or serial cable to the ARHP PC
Audio requires an analogue cable from radio's ACC 2 connector to the ARHP PC sound card

stationTarget.label: SCU-LAN10 IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: The SCU-LAN10 interface has its own LAN address, separate from the radio. Traffic leaves the tunnel and goes to this address.
stationTarget.howToFind: Use the SCU-LAN10 Setting Tool to view or set the IP address. Set it to static.
stationTarget.ifWrong: All rules will show 'Listening' but the Remote Software will time out connecting.

clientNotes: SCU-LAN10 Remote Software -> IP Address: 127.0.0.1
Port settings must match (50000-50003 by default)
No public IP or dynamic DNS is needed -- RWK provides the tunnel
radioNotes: SCU-LAN10 must be connected to the radio and powered on
Set a static IP address via the SCU-LAN10 Setting Tool

stationTarget.label: FlexRadio IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: SmartSDR connects to the radio's command port. The discovery relay handles finding the radio, but the forward rule still needs the radio's address.
stationTarget.howToFind: Check SmartSDR on the Station PC, or look at the radio's front panel under Network settings.
stationTarget.ifWrong: SmartSDR will discover the radio (via the relay) but fail to connect to it.

clientNotes: IMPORTANT: Enable 'discovery re-emission' on the Client (FlexRadio Discovery panel)
SmartSDR will discover the radio automatically once the relay and forwards are active
No SmartLink account is needed
stationNotes: IMPORTANT: Enable 'discovery capture' on the Station
The Station captures VITA-49 discovery broadcasts and relays them to the Client
radioNotes: Set a static IP address on the radio

stationTarget.label: K4 IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: The K4 runs its own remote server. One TCP connection carries everything (commands, audio, panadapter).
stationTarget.howToFind: On the K4: CONFIG -> NETWORK. Note the IP address shown.
stationTarget.ifWrong: QK4 / Virtual K4 will fail to connect.

clientNotes: QK4 or Virtual K4 -> Server address: 127.0.0.1, port 9205
Only ONE rule is needed -- the K4 multiplexes everything on one TCP port
radioNotes: Enable Remote Server in the K4's CONFIG -> NETWORK menu

stationTarget.label: Radio-RRC IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: The Radio-RRC box sits on the Station's LAN next to the radio. It has its own IP address.
stationTarget.howToFind: Check the Radio-RRC's web interface (default http://192.168.1.3) or use the RemoteRig IP scanning tool.
stationTarget.ifWrong: SIP registration will fail. The Control-RRC at your operating position will show 'No connection'.

clientNotes: IMPORTANT: These rules bind to 0.0.0.0, which means they are accessible from your LAN
Point your Control-RRC hardware at this PC's LAN IP address (not 127.0.0.1)
Ensure SIP ALG is disabled on your client-side router
radioNotes: Radio-RRC must have a static IP address on the Station's LAN

stationTarget.label: rigctld host address
stationTarget.why: rigctld listens on this address at the Station. Usually 127.0.0.1 if it runs on the Station PC.
stationTarget.howToFind: If rigctld runs on the Station PC: 127.0.0.1. If on another device, use that device's LAN IP.

clientNotes: Configure your logger/software to connect to 127.0.0.1:4532 for CAT
stationNotes: rigctld must be running on the Station PC

stationTarget.label: rotctld host address
stationTarget.why: rotctld listens on this address at the Station.
stationTarget.howToFind: If rotctld runs on the Station PC: 127.0.0.1.

clientNotes: Configure your rotator control software to connect to 127.0.0.1:4533
stationNotes: rotctld must be running on the Station PC

stationTarget.label: RDP target address
stationTarget.why: Remote Desktop runs on the Station PC. Usually 127.0.0.1.
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 if connecting to the Station PC itself.
stationTarget.ifWrong: Remote Desktop will fail to connect.

clientNotes: Remote Desktop Connection -> Computer: 127.0.0.1
stationNotes: Remote Desktop must be enabled on the Station PC (Settings -> System -> Remote Desktop)

stationTarget.label: VNC server address
stationTarget.why: VNC server runs on the Station PC.
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 if VNC is on the Station PC.
stationTarget.ifWrong: VNC viewer will fail to connect.

clientNotes: VNC Viewer -> Server: 127.0.0.1:5900
stationNotes: VNC server must be running on the Station PC

stationTarget.label: PstRotator host address
stationTarget.why: PstRotator listens for TCP connections on this address.
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 if PstRotator runs on the Station PC.

clientNotes: Configure your rotator control to connect to 127.0.0.1:12000
stationNotes: PstRotator must be running with TCP server enabled

stationTarget.label: Serial bridge target address
stationTarget.why: The TCP serial server (VSPE TcpServer, com2tcp, or ser2net) listens on this address at the Station.
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 if the serial server runs on the Station PC itself.
stationTarget.ifWrong: The virtual COM port on the client will not connect.

basePort.label: TCP port for the serial bridge
basePort.why: Each serial device needs its own TCP port. Default starts at 4000 and increments.
basePort.howToFind: Use any available port. 4000 is a good default for the first device.
basePort.ifWrong: Port conflict -- another service may already be using that port.

clientNotes: Install VSPE or com0com on this PC
Create a TcpClient virtual COM port pointing at 127.0.0.1:<port>
Configure your logger to use the virtual COM port
stationNotes: Install VSPE or com2tcp on the Station PC
Create a TcpServer listening on 0.0.0.0:<port> connected to the real COM port
Match baud rate, data bits, parity, stop bits to the device

stationTarget.label: Service target address
stationTarget.why: Where does this service listen on the Station's network?
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 if it's on the Station PC. Otherwise, the device's LAN IP.
stationTarget.ifWrong: Connection will time out or be refused.

clientNotes: Connect your client software to 127.0.0.1:<port>
stationNotes: Ensure the target service is running and accessible
